title: Cold rebuild: Next version from commits
summary: Rebuild Next version from commits from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Next version from commits** in *Tags, releases and branching strategies*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: You run `git tag -a v2.0.0 -m "2.0"` and then `git push`. Your colleague does `git fetch` and cannot see the tag. Why?
options: Plain `git push` does not push tags; run `git push origin v2.0.0` or `git push --follow-tags`
steps.explain: Branches and tags are pushed separately. Teams often set `git config --global push.followTags true`.

steps.title: Rebuild Next version from commits cold
prompt: Write `NextVersion(string current, List<string> subjects)` for Conventional Commits:
- **Breaking** if any subject contains `BREAKING CHANGE`, or its type (the part before the first `:`) ends with `!` (like `feat!:` or `fix(api)!:`). Then `v<major+1>.0.0`.
- Else if any subject starts with `feat`: `v<major>.<minor+1>.0`.
- Else if any subject starts with `fix`: bump patch.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
static string NextVersion(string current, List<string> subjects)
